Closing note, 22:30 sim. Three weather cells over the Canaries, Madeira and the Valencia coast slotted our morning wave and the delays rolled through the fleet as late aircraft all day, with 3,135 bags short-shipped behind the rushed turns. I answered all 159 decisions and defaulted none: took slots under 20 minutes and sent REA on the rest (every REA got an improvement), announced every delay so passengers heard first, rushed every bag, held fares on eight cuts and matched three where loads were soft and the cut shallow, and never cancelled a flight or lost a crew. Jet2 finishes top of the lobby at 139.6 with zero cancellations against Aer Lingus 138.8, Flybe 138.1 and Air France 138.0, all autopilot carriers, and against the 126 to 139 band the autopilot produced across the field; the bag bill of 47m is the price of the weather rather than of any choice, though next time I would retime the tightest regulated turns pre-emptively to leave fewer bags on the ramp, and watch the LS254 and LS335 tails earlier for the four-hour delays that built up unnoticed.
